sentences.text: Lourinhasaurus was a heavy-bodied herbivore with a long neck that reached about 17 meters in length.
This animal is estimated to have reached 15 to 18 meters in length and weighed around 5 metric tons, with a femur estimated to be 1.68 meters long.
The name Lourinhasaurus means "lizard from Lourinhã," even though the type specimen was not found in that municipality.
The first fossil remains were discovered in June 1949 by American geologist Harold Weston Robbins near Alenquer.
The Moinho do Carmo specimen was designated the lectotype for Lourinhasaurus alenquerensis in 2003.
Lourinhasaurus was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur that lived in the Late Jurassic of Portugal.
Lourinhasaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Lourinhasaurus is a basal Macronarian closely related to Camarasaurus, and it belongs to the family Camarasauridae, which is its parent group.
Lourinhasaurus lived approximately 150 to 145 million years ago during the Late Jurassic, spanning the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, specifically from 152.21 to 145.06 million years ago.

The classification of Lourinhasaurus has been controversial, with some specimens originally referred to it later reinterpreted as belonging to other genera like Dinheirosaurus, and the Porto Dinheiro specimen, initially used to define Lourinhasaurus, was later reinterpreted as a diplodocid named Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis. It is debated whether the second specimen should be classified as Lourinhasaurus or the separate genus Dinheirosaurus.
